leftEvidence.title: Moses is a shepherd asking “Who am I?”

points.label: Setting
points.left: Moses tends Jethro’s flock in the wilderness when he is called.
points.right: Moses stands inside a complaining camp carrying a people he says are too heavy for him.

points.label: Self-question
points.left: “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh?”
points.right: “I am not able to bear all this people alone.”

points.label: Answer around him
points.left: The call answers inadequacy with divine presence: “I will be with you.”
points.right: The burden is answered by sharing responsibility with seventy elders.

points.label: Image
points.left: Moses begins as an actual shepherd.
points.right: Moses describes carrying Israel with parental imagery; later he will ask for a shepherd successor.

payload.posture: Hold the shepherd Moses before his public mission beside the leader who later says he cannot carry the people alone.

rightEvidence.title: Moses says the people are too heavy to carry alone

payload.tension: Hold the shepherd Moses before his public mission beside the leader who later says he cannot carry the people alone.
payload.title: Shepherd at Horeb / burdened in the camp
